# Skeleton accessibility conformance

Rated against WCAG 2.2 Level A and AA. See the [reports legend](../accessibility.md).

## Known gaps

- ⚠️ **2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide.** <!-- 2.2.2:gap:start -->The `pulse` and `wave` animations run indefinitely by default, with no end-user control to pause or hide them. The author can set `animation={false}`, use `motion.reducedMotion`, or remove the placeholder once loading finishes.<!-- 2.2.2:gap:end -->
- ⚠️ **4.1.3 Status Messages.** <!-- 4.1.3:gap:start -->The loading state and its completion are not announced. The author sets `aria-busy` on the surrounding region and adds a polite live region where the update must be heard.<!-- 4.1.3:gap:end -->

## Success criteria

### 🔍 Manual

#### 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast · AA

`🚩` · `✅ Supports` · `● Component`

<!-- 1.4.11:start -->

- A `Skeleton` is a placeholder that stands in for content that has not loaded. It carries no information of its own and is not a control, so the contrast requirement for graphical objects needed to understand the content does not apply to it. The loaded content must meet the criteria in its own report.
- Measured from the default theme, the fill is `text.primary` at `0.11` alpha in light mode and `0.13` in dark mode: `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.11)` on `#fff` is `#e3e3e3`, about `1.28:1`; `rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.13)` on `#121212` is `#313131`, about `1.44:1`. At the trough of the `pulse` animation (`opacity: 0.4`), about `1.10:1` light and `1.12:1` dark. The [Accessibility](https://mui.com/material-ui/react-skeleton/#accessibility) docs say the color uses the least luminance to be visible in good conditions, so a user with a low-vision need may not see the placeholder at all.
- A placeholder that is not seen costs a user the cue that content is on its way. That is why 4.1.3 carries the loading state for assistive technology, and why an author who needs the placeholder to be seen can raise the contrast with the `bgcolor` in `sx`.

**Manual testing steps**

1. With a contrast checker (the color picker in browser DevTools shows a ratio), measure a `Skeleton` fill against the page in light and dark mode.
2. Record the ratio and confirm the region also tells assistive technology that content is loading, per 4.1.3.
3. Check any custom `bgcolor` the application sets.

<!-- 1.4.11:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 1.4.11:pass:start -->the placeholder is decorative and not required to understand the content, so it is not held to `3:1`. Its default fill is below `3:1` (about `1.28:1` light, `1.44:1` dark) by design.<!-- 1.4.11:pass:end -->

#### 2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide · A

`🚩` · `⚠️ Partially Supports` · `◐ Shared`

<!-- 2.2.2:start -->

- `animation="pulse"` (the default) fades the fill between `opacity: 1` and `0.4` and back over `2s`, and `animation="wave"` sweeps a highlight across over `2s`. Both are infinite CSS animations (`2s … 0.5s infinite`) that start automatically, so a placeholder that stays on screen for more than five seconds runs the animation for longer than five seconds alongside other content.
- The component gives the end user no control to pause, stop or hide the motion. The author has three ways to remove it: `animation={false}` renders a static placeholder; `motion.reducedMotion: 'system'` removes it for users whose OS asks for reduced motion, and `'always'` removes it for everyone (unit tests assert `'always'`); the placeholder disappears when the content loads. The default `motion.reducedMotion` is `never`, so the OS preference is not honored by default.
- 2.2.2 is a Level A requirement for motion that lasts more than five seconds, and the sufficient techniques call for a control or for the motion to stop. The default does neither, so the rating is Partially Supports until the author takes one of the three steps above.

**Manual testing steps**

1. Render a `Skeleton` with the default animation and another with `animation="wave"` on a page with other content, and leave them for more than five seconds.
2. Look for a way to pause, stop or hide the motion.
3. Set `animation={false}` and confirm the placeholder is static.
4. Set the OS "reduce motion" preference and confirm whether the animation stops. It stops only when the theme sets `motion.reducedMotion: 'system'`.

<!-- 2.2.2:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 2.2.2:pass:start -->the user can pause, stop or hide the motion, or it stops within five seconds. The component supplies no such control; `animation={false}`, `motion.reducedMotion`, or removing the placeholder once content arrives is what keeps it conformant.<!-- 2.2.2:pass:end -->

#### 2.3.1 Three Flashes or Below Threshold · A

`🚩` · `✅ Supports` · `● Component`

<!-- 2.3.1:start -->

- `pulse` crosses its full opacity range once every `2s` (`0.5 Hz`), and `wave` sweeps once every `2s` followed by a `0.5s` delay. Nothing flashes, and nothing repeats three times in one second. The `pulse` swing is `1` to `0.4` of a fill that is already about `1.28:1` against the page, so the change in luminance is small.

**Manual testing steps**

1. Watch a `Skeleton` with `pulse` and one with `wave` for any part that flashes more than three times in any one second.

<!-- 2.3.1:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 2.3.1:pass:start -->no part flashes more than three times per second.<!-- 2.3.1:pass:end -->

#### 4.1.3 Status Messages · AA

`🚩` · `⚠️ Partially Supports` · `◐ Shared`

<!-- 4.1.3:start -->

- The component adds no `role`, no `aria-busy` and no live region. A screen reader user is told nothing when placeholders appear, and nothing when real content replaces them, so the loading state and its completion are not announced unless the surrounding application adds them.
- The author marks the loading region with `aria-busy="true"` and sets it back to `false` (or removes it) when the content arrives. Whether a change inside an `aria-busy` region is announced varies between screen readers and browsers; where the update must be heard, add a polite live region (the W3C `ARIA19` and `ARIA22` patterns for status messages) to the application. `aria-busy` is an advisory state and does not guarantee an announcement.

**Manual testing steps**

1. With a screen reader running (NVDA with Chrome, or VoiceOver with Safari), read a region that shows `Skeleton` placeholders. Record what is announced. Repeat with `aria-busy="true"` on the region.
2. Replace the placeholders with the content. Record whether the change is announced without the user moving focus.
3. If it is not, add a polite live region that announces the loaded state and repeat.

<!-- 4.1.3:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 4.1.3:pass:start -->the loaded content is announced without the user moving focus to it. It is not by default; set `aria-busy` on the region and add a polite live region in the application to convey it.<!-- 4.1.3:pass:end -->

### 🔁 Hybrid

#### 1.3.1 Info and Relationships · A

`✅ Supports` · `● Component`

Tested by: unit `Skeleton.test.js`

<!-- 1.3.1:start -->

- The root is a plain `<span>` (or the `component` the author passes). It sets no `role` and no `aria-*` attribute, so a placeholder contributes nothing to the accessibility tree. In Chromium's accessibility tree a `Skeleton` is absent, and a `Skeleton` that wraps children hides them with `visibility: hidden`, which also removes them from the tree. A unit test asserts that no role or ARIA attribute is added.
- The relationship the placeholder stands for, "this region is loading content", is not conveyed by the component. The author states it on the surrounding region with `aria-busy`, as the [Accessibility](https://mui.com/material-ui/react-skeleton/#accessibility) docs leave to the author. Announcing the change is rated under 4.1.3.
- axe-core `aria-allowed-attr`, `aria-conditional-attr`, `aria-prohibited-attr`, `aria-valid-attr` and `aria-valid-attr-value` pass across the demos and fixtures in [`skeleton.a11y.json`](../../../../docs/data/material/components/skeleton/skeleton.a11y.json), including a `section` marked `aria-busy`.

**Manual testing steps**

1. In the accessibility tree (in Chrome DevTools: Elements panel, Accessibility tab), inspect a region that shows `Skeleton` placeholders, including one that wraps an `Avatar` or `Typography`.
2. Confirm the placeholders do not appear as nodes, and that wrapped children are not exposed.
3. With a screen reader, move through the region and confirm nothing is read for the placeholders.

<!-- 1.3.1:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 1.3.1:pass:start -->the placeholders and any wrapped children are not exposed, and the region carries the busy state when the author sets `aria-busy`.<!-- 1.3.1:pass:end -->

## Not applicable

- **1.1.1 Non-text Content (A).** <!-- 1.1.1:start -->The component renders no image, icon or text. It is an empty placeholder with no text alternative to provide; the content it stands in for supplies its own once loaded.<!-- 1.1.1:end -->
- **1.2.1 Audio-only and Video-only (Prerecorded) (A), 1.2.2 Captions (Prerecorded) (A), 1.2.3 Audio Description or Media Alternative (Prerecorded) (A), 1.2.4 Captions (Live) (AA), 1.2.5 Audio Description (Prerecorded) (AA).** No audio or video.
- **1.3.2 Meaningful Sequence (A), 1.3.3 Sensory Characteristics (A).** <!-- 1.3.2,1.3.3:start -->A single empty placeholder with no reading order of its own, no instruction and no sensory characteristic to rely on. The order of placeholders follows the author's layout.<!-- 1.3.2,1.3.3:end -->
- **1.3.4 Orientation (AA).** Sets no orientation lock; a layout concern.
- **1.3.5 Identify Input Purpose (AA).** Collects no information about the user through `autocomplete`.
- **1.4.1 Use of Color (A).** <!-- 1.4.1:start -->Color carries no information. The placeholder's fill is a neutral tint, and whether content is loading is not encoded in a color change.<!-- 1.4.1:end -->
- **1.4.2 Audio Control (A).** Emits no audio.
- **1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum) (AA), 1.4.4 Resize Text (AA), 1.4.5 Images of Text (AA), 1.4.12 Text Spacing (AA).** <!-- 1.4.3,1.4.4,1.4.5,1.4.12:start -->The component renders no text and no image of text. A wrapped child is `visibility: hidden`, so it is not rendered to the user. A `variant="text"` placeholder takes its height from the font size (`1.2em`), which is a sizing relationship rather than text that can be resized or respaced.<!-- 1.4.3,1.4.4,1.4.5,1.4.12:end -->
- **1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus (AA).** Shows no additional content on hover or focus; a `Tooltip` wrapper would own this.
- **2.1.1 Keyboard (A), 2.1.2 No Keyboard Trap (A), 2.4.3 Focus Order (A), 2.4.7 Focus Visible (AA), 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum) (AA), 3.2.1 On Focus (A).** <!-- 2.1.1,2.1.2,2.4.3,2.4.7,2.4.11,3.2.1:start -->The placeholder is not focusable or interactive: it sets no `tabIndex`, takes no keyboard input, and never receives focus, so it cannot trap focus, enter the focus order, show a focus indicator, have focus obscured, or change context on focus.<!-- 2.1.1,2.1.2,2.4.3,2.4.7,2.4.11,3.2.1:end -->
- **2.1.4 Character Key Shortcuts (A).** Binds no single-character keyboard shortcut.
- **2.2.1 Timing Adjustable (A).** Sets no time limit.
- **2.4.1 Bypass Blocks (A), 2.4.2 Page Titled (A), 2.4.5 Multiple Ways (AA).** Page or site structure, not a single component.
- **2.4.4 Link Purpose (In Context) (A).** The component renders no links.
- **2.4.6 Headings and Labels (AA), 3.2.4 Consistent Identification (AA), 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (A).** <!-- 2.4.6,3.2.4,4.1.2:start -->The placeholder has no name, role or value to expose and is not a heading, label or identifiable control. The loading state belongs on the surrounding region, rated under 1.3.1 and 4.1.3.<!-- 2.4.6,3.2.4,4.1.2:end -->
- **2.5.1 Pointer Gestures (A), 2.5.4 Motion Actuation (A).** Activates on a simple click; reads no device motion.
- **2.5.2 Pointer Cancellation (A), 2.5.3 Label in Name (A), 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum) (AA), 3.2.2 On Input (A), 3.3.2 Labels or Instructions (A).** <!-- 2.5.2,2.5.3,2.5.8,3.2.2,3.3.2:start -->Not an interactive target and not an input: no pointer events to cancel, no label text, no activation target, no change on input, and no field to label or give instructions for.<!-- 2.5.2,2.5.3,2.5.8,3.2.2,3.3.2:end -->
- **2.5.7 Dragging Movements (AA).** No drag interactions.
- **3.1.1 Language of Page (A), 3.1.2 Language of Parts (AA).** The component emits no `<html lang>` and no text of its own. A foreign-language label is the author's phrase to mark.
- **3.2.3 Consistent Navigation (AA).** Covers repeated navigation across a set of pages, not a single component.
- **3.2.6 Consistent Help (A).** Covers consistent placement of help across pages.
- **3.3.1 Error Identification (A), 3.3.3 Error Suggestion (AA), 3.3.4 Error Prevention (Legal, Financial, Data) (AA).** Collects and validates no input; these belong to the form or process.
- **3.3.7 Redundant Entry (A).** Captures no previously entered data to repopulate.
- **3.3.8 Accessible Authentication (Minimum) (AA).** No authentication step; the duty falls on the credential fields.

## Level AAA

<!-- level-aaa:start -->

- **2.3.3 Animation from Interactions.** The `pulse` and `wave` animations reduce only via `motion.reducedMotion`: `system` follows the OS `prefers-reduced-motion` query and `always` removes the animation unconditionally; the default `never` does not, so OS reduced-motion is not honored by default. `🚩`
- **2.4.12 Focus Not Obscured (Enhanced), 2.4.13 Focus Appearance, 2.5.5 Target Size (Enhanced).** Not focusable and not an activation target.
- **1.4.6 Contrast (Enhanced).** Renders no text.

<!-- level-aaa:end -->

## Scope and test environment

- **Standard.** WCAG 2.2, Level A and AA.
- **Component version.** `@mui/material` 10.0.0-alpha.0.

<!-- scope:start -->

- **Scope.** The Skeleton component in isolation, rendered through its documented API. A `Skeleton` that wraps children is covered for how it hides them; the wrapped content is the author's.
- **Automated.** axe-core via the Playwright harness (results in [`skeleton.a11y.json`](../../../../docs/data/material/components/skeleton/skeleton.a11y.json)) on the `Animations`, `SkeletonColor`, `SkeletonTypography` and `Variants` docs demos and on two a11y fixtures, plus component unit tests. The `SkeletonChildren`, `Facebook` and `YouTube` demos load remote images and are not enrolled.
- **Assistive-technology review.** Not yet performed. Flagged criteria are assessed from source and the Chromium accessibility tree, pending a review with NVDA, JAWS and VoiceOver.

<!-- scope:end -->
